gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: feeling unwell for 8 days. Generated CC: 1-week sore throat progressing to dry cough and request for note/meds. Duration of general malaise (8 days) is not explicitly stated.
Gold: illness began with sore throat then progressed to dry cough. Gen hpi-001: sore throat then 1–2 days later a dry, non-productive cough. Same sequence and type of cough; added timing detail only.
Gold: cough is non-productive with no sputum. Gen hpi-001 and hpi-009: dry, non-productive cough and denies purulent sputum. Together they capture non-productive/no sputum.
Gold: no blood in the cough. Gen hpi-008: denies coughing up blood. Equivalent.
Gold: patient denies chest pain. Gen hpi-002: reports chest pain for 3–4 days. Direct conflict.
Gold: mild SOB, not at rest, not limiting activity. Gen hpi-002 and hpi-003: SOB with exertional symptoms, not limiting, can climb stairs. Same clinical idea.
Gold: slight fever symptoms. Gen hpi-004: fever first 3 days then resolved. This specifies definite fever, not slight fever symptoms; nuance differs, so gold description is not exactly captured.
Gold: symptoms are gradually improving. Gen hpi-007: symptoms fluctuate in better/worse cycles. Fluctuation vs steady gradual improvement are clinically different and conflicting descriptions.
Gold: reduced appetite. Gen hpi-006: decreased appetite. Equivalent.
Gold: denies unintentional weight loss. Gen hpi-006: decreased appetite without weight loss. Same core fact (no weight loss).
Gold: denies history of asthma. No generated fact mentions asthma.

Gold: no significant past medical history (no sig PHMx). Gen pmh-001: no past medical or surgical history. This escalates from 'no significant' to 'none at all', which can conflict if there are minor conditions not considered significant. Given auditing rigor, treat as contradiction.
Gold: no significant regular medications. Gen med-001: no medications. This is stronger than 'no significant'; some meds might exist but be non-significant. Does not exactly capture the gold fact.

Gold: no known drug allergies (NKDA). Gen allergy-001: peanut (food) allergy. Presence of a food allergy conflicts with 'no known drug allergies' only if NKDA was intended as general allergy-free; however, in strict terms NKDA refers to drugs and peanut is a food, so this is better classified as ADDITION than direct contradiction. But peanut allergy is not a drug allergy, so there is actually no direct opposition; status should not be contradicted. (However your schema only allows COVERED/OMITTED here, so strictly: it is OMITTED as NKDA is not expressed.)
Gold: mother had lung cancer. Gen fh-001: mother has lung cancer. Same relationship and condition.
Gold: patient is a non-smoker. Gen sh-001: non-smoker who experimented once or twice. Still categorized as non-smoker; consistent and includes extra detail.
Gold: no asbestos exposure. Gen sh-002: no asbestos exposure. Identical.

Gold: no significant recent travel history. Gen hpi-011: denies recent exotic travel. This narrows the denial to exotic travel rather than all significant travel; these can conflict (a non-exotic but significant trip would be captured in gold but not in generated).
Gold: on exam, patient looks well. No generated physical exam findings are provided.
Gold: patient advised no formal work certificate required; can self-certify. Gen plan-004: sick note will be provided for additional days off work. This is opposite advice regarding certification.

Gold: review if worsening symptoms, especially sudden change in SOB. Gen plan-003: ED/GP if increased SOB, new/worse chest pain, sustained fever, no improvement >1 wk. Worsening SOB trigger is present, matching the core gold instruction.

Gold: expected to be better in 5 days; review if not better then. Gen plan-001/plan-002: expect improvement within ≤5 days; and plan-003: seek review if no improvement >1 week. The explicit 5-day review threshold is slightly shifted but expectation of improvement by ~5 days is captured; follow-up threshold is more conservative. For coverage of expectation, this is acceptable.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold CC only states feeling unwell for 8 days. Generated CC adds sore throat/dry cough details and requests for reassurance, meds, and sick note, none of which are in the gold chief complaint.
Sequence sore throat → dry, non-productive cough matches gold; added onset timing detail.
Gen: SOB with mild wheeze and chest pain for 3–4 days. Gold: mild SOB only and explicit denial of chest pain (hpi-004); no wheeze mentioned. This conflicts with gold denial of chest pain.

Exertional SOB not limiting and able to climb stairs is consistent with gold hpi-005 (mild SOB, not at rest, not limiting). However, this fact is bundled with chest symptoms that contradict gold; the SOB component is supported, chest component is not. If forced classification, treat the SOB description as SUPPORTED by hpi-005 and the added chest symptom piece as CONTRADICTORY to hpi-004.
Gen: definite fever for first 3 days, now resolved. Gold only states slight fever symptoms without duration or resolution. This is extra temporal detail and strength of fever, not present in gold.
Intermittent headaches are not mentioned anywhere in the gold facts.

Decreased appetite without weight loss: decreased appetite is supported by gold hpi-008; absence of weight loss is supported by gold hpi-009. Combined, content is consistent but gold does not explicitly link them in a single statement. Overall compatible and can be considered SUPPORTED by both hpi-008 and hpi-009.
Gen: symptoms fluctuate in better/worse cycles. Gold hpi-007: symptoms are gradually improving. Fluctuating course vs gradual improvement are conflicting descriptions.
Denies coughing up blood matches gold 'No blood in cough.'
Denies purulent sputum is consistent with non-productive cough and no sputum in gold; does not conflict and refines it.
Denial of sinus congestion is not present in the gold facts.
Gen: denies recent exotic travel. Gold sh-003: no significant recent travel history (not limited to exotic). The narrower gen denial potentially conflicts with the broader gold statement.
Gen: no past medical or surgical history. Gold pmh-002: no significant past medical history, which allows minor issues. The absolute 'none' may contradict the qualified 'no significant.'
Gen: no medications. Gold med-001: no significant regular medications, which permits minor or non-regular meds. The generated absolute statement is stronger and may conflict if such meds exist.
Gen: peanut (food) allergy. Gold only states NKDA (drug allergies). Food allergy status is not addressed in gold, so this is additional information, not a direct contradiction to no drug allergies.
Mother with lung cancer is exactly in gold.
No family history of DVT/PE is not mentioned in any gold fact.
Non-smoker status matches gold; experimentation detail is additional but consistent.
No asbestos exposure is directly in gold.
Birth in US and 12 years in UK are social details absent from gold.
Employment status is not documented in the gold facts.
Assessment of probable viral URTI/pharyngitis with dry cough and mild SOB/wheeze is not present in the gold, which has no assessment/diagnosis section.
Work absence secondary to illness is not mentioned in gold.
Health anxiety regarding lung cancer and TB is not in the gold facts.
Paracetamol PRN, fluids, rest are new management details; gold plan only discusses work certification and follow-up, not medications or fluids/rest.

Gen: expect improvement within five days. Gold fu-002: expect to improve and be better in 5 days. This part is supported. However, gold also ties this to review if not better at that time, which gen defers to >1 week in plan-003, so follow-up threshold differs.

Safety-netting for ↑SOB aligns with gold fu-001. However, gen adds triggers (new/worse chest pain, sustained fever, no improvement >1 wk) and sets review at >1 week instead of specifically 5 days as in gold fu-002. Both supported and additional elements are present; the longer threshold is looser than gold.
Gen: sick note will be provided. Gold plan-001: formal work certificate not required; patient can self-certify. Directly conflicting plan regarding certification.
Reassurance about low likelihood of malignancy/TB and re-review if persistent symptoms are not mentioned in any gold fact.
